themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions in Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights have spiked dramatically THIS WEEK to 35 complaints vs. a baseline of 6.1 per week—a 471% surge (z-score: 6.74)—suggesting rapid deterioration of roadbeds, potholes, or asphalt failure affecting resident mobility and safety.
evidence: 35 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.1-complaint weekly average over prior 8 weeks (471% spike)
Z-score of 6.74 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
Aligns with recurring CB budget request for increased sanitation and street maintenance funding
reporting_angles: On-the-ground survey of specific blocks with potholes or failed asphalt; visual documentation of worst-affected areas
Interview DOT/Sanitation officials about why THIS specific week saw such a sharp spike—weather event, deferred maintenance, or staffing issue?

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints surged THIS WEEK to 93 vs. a baseline of 22.5 per week—a 313% spike (z-score: 5.53)—suggesting new construction, restaurant/bar activity, or delivery operations concentrating in the district.
evidence: 93 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 22.5-complaint weekly average over prior 8 weeks (313% spike)
Z-score of 5.53 indicates highly statistically significant anomaly
Coincides with 336 DOB filings in past 90 days (295 alterations) suggesting active construction/business renovation activity
reporting_angles: Map the 93 complaints geographically—are they clustered near Amsterdam Avenue, 125th Street corridor, or specific venues?
Identify which new businesses, construction sites, or venues opened/expanded in the past 2 weeks; interview affected residents about sleep disruption and quality of life

themes_detail.label: Elevator System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints spiked THIS WEEK to 6 vs. a baseline of 1.6 per week—a 269% increase (z-score: 5.11)—indicating potential systemic failures in residential buildings or possibly elevated demand due to heat-related complaints.
evidence: 6 elevator complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6-complaint weekly average over prior 8 weeks (269% spike)
Z-score of 5.11 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Occurs alongside context of 5,470 heat/hot water complaints (highest overall category) and 295 building alterations, both of which may stress elevator systems
reporting_angles: Identify which residential buildings are repeat offenders; interview residents about wait times, frequency of breakdowns, and impact on elderly/disabled tenants
Contact DOB and NYC Department of Buildings to understand maintenance inspection patterns and whether there are systemic failures in the district

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Animal Crisis (2 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal/private property complaints spiked 2 WEEKS AGO to 3 vs. a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—though this spike has now aged; warrants follow-up to determine if the underlying issue (pest/animal infestation) has been resolved.
evidence: 3 unsanitary animal complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2-complaint weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Aligns with recurring CB budget request for animal and pest control including rat and mosquito reduction
reporting_angles: Follow-up investigation: have these 3 cases been resolved, or do complaints persist in a new week's count?
Broader story on rat/pest control in the district; interview DOHMH on whether there is a documented infestation trend

themes_detail.label: Flooring/Stairs Deterioration (3 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Flooring and stair complaints spiked 3 WEEKS AGO to 39 vs. a baseline of 16.1 per week—a 142% increase (z-score: 4.54)—suggesting aging building stock or deferred maintenance in residential units, though this spike is older than current week anomalies.
evidence: 39 flooring/stair complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 16.1-complaint weekly average over prior 8 weeks (142% spike)
Z-score of 4.54 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Consistent with broader pattern of aging building stock (295 alterations filed in past 90 days suggest reactive maintenance mode)
reporting_angles: Verify whether this spike has normalized in the current week or if it represents sustained deterioration
Feature story on aging building stock in Morningside Heights; interview residents about safety hazards and landlord responsiveness
